newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finmin calm on zloty fall, expects rebound.
newsitem.headline: Polish finmin calm on zloty fall, expects rebound.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Marek Belka said the zloty's recent sharp fall was caused by speculation rather than bad fundamentals and it should start to firm again soon.
He said in a radio interview on Thursday that the zloty's rise on Wednesday, which followed dollar-selling intervention by the National Bank of Poland, proved its earlier losses were unfounded.

"It was not foreign investors, it seems, who were fleeing the zloty but domestic traders who went wild and began moving from zlotys to dollars. I watch it with calm...I think it will now reverse," he declared.

The zloty plunged by five percent on Tuesday against a basket of currencies to a fixing of 5.69 percent below the parity rate, It rebounded to 3.41 percent below parity on Wednedsay after the central bank sold $5 million on the market.

Analysts said the fall was propelled by fears, both in Poland and abroad, that the government's flood relief spending would boost domestic demand and imports, widening an already big trade deficit and possibly increasing inflation.
Heavy rains in southern Poland have caused floods which put more than 4,000 sq km under water, killed at least 39 people and forced tens of thousands from their homes.
